title: Safe use and care of electrical machines
audience: Cleaners and supervisors who operate, move or store electrical cleaning equipment in any cleaning-group business.
learningOutcomes: Complete a pre-use safety check on an electrical machine, covering its test label, plug, flex and casing.
Connect and disconnect a machine using the socket-switch sequence.
Route the flex so it cannot be run over, caught or damaged while the machine is operating.
Tag a faulty machine, remove it from service and report it.
Explain why repairs to fixed wiring or to a machine's internal parts are outside a cleaner's role.

instruction.heading: Why electrical equipment needs a routine check
instruction.body: Electrical cleaning machines combine water, moving parts and long cables, and each of these creates a route to injury. Faults usually start small: a nicked flex, a cracked plug, or a filter packed with fine dust that makes a motor run hot. The source sets a pre-use routine and a rule that only trained people operate electrical equipment. Your part is to look, feel and listen before the machine is switched on, and to stop the moment something is wrong. The checks are short, but a fault that was missed in a two-minute check can become a shock in the middle of a job.

instruction.heading: Test labels and the pre-use check
instruction.body: Each machine should carry a label showing when it was last tested and when the next test is due. The source calls this a PAT test. Read the date on the label first. Then run your hand along the flex from the plug to the machine, looking for cuts, flattened sections, bare wires, or electrical tape standing in for a repair. Check the plug and pins for scorch marks, bent pins or cracks. Look at the casing for cracks, and check the bag or filter, because a blocked filter can make the machine overheat. The source requires a register listing all machines, so record the check.

instruction.heading: Connecting, running and disconnecting
instruction.body: Before you plug in, make sure the socket switch is off. Plug in, then switch on. When you have finished, switch the socket off before you unplug the machine from the wall. Keep the flex behind you while you work, so you are never walking over it or dragging it through a wet area. Where a flex must cross a walkway, make the crossing safe with a cable cover or a clear route, and let the supervisor know. Check that the building has a protective device, such as a circuit breaker or safety switch, that cuts supply if a fault occurs. The source states that circuit breakers are expected to be fitted.

instruction.heading: Faults, storage and who fixes what
instruction.body: A machine with a fault is not used. Tag it as faulty, remove it from service, and report it to your line manager. Do not tape over damaged flex, and do not open a casing to look inside. Repairs go to an approved contractor, as the source requires for checking and repair. Store machines upright, with the cable loosely coiled and not trailing. Wet or dusty machines are dried and wiped down before they are put away. Work on fixed wiring, power points or building circuits is licensed electrical work and is outside this lesson; the licence notice in this lesson explains the boundary.

instruction.heading: Protective equipment and ventilation
instruction.body: Wear gloves and full enclosed shoes when you use electrical equipment, because the source identifies hand and foot injury as the risk. Gloves are also worn when you handle bags and filters. Add eye protection when dust or product spray is present. Open windows or doors where possible, so that any fumes from products used with the machine do not build up around you or the customer.

procedure: Read the test label and confirm the next due date has not passed before the machine is used.
Run a hand along the flex from plug to machine, then check the plug, pins and casing for damage.
Check the bag or filter and empty or replace it as needed. Confirm any brush or pad attachment is correctly fitted.
Confirm the socket switch is off, then plug the machine in.
Keep the flex behind you and out of walkways and wet areas during operation.
If the machine sounds different, loses suction or runs hot, stop it, switch off the socket and unplug before checking.
Switch the socket off before unplugging. Coil the flex loosely and store the machine upright.
Tag and report any fault, and update the equipment register with the check.

workedExamples.situation: Partway through a commercial floor clean, the vacuum starts to smell warm, and the flex has a patch of tape near the plug.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What do you do with the machine and the job?
workedExamples.reasoning: Switch the socket off and unplug the machine. Do not run it again, and do not repair the flex with tape. Tag the machine as faulty, remove it from service, and report it to your line manager. Record the time and the condition you found. Move the job to an approved machine only if the supervisor agrees.

workedExamples.situation: A supervisor asks you to use a machine whose next test date has already passed, and says it still runs well.
workedExamples.reasoning: No. A machine past its test date is not treated as safe to use until it has been tested. A machine that runs well may still have a fault you cannot see. Tell the supervisor, tag the machine, and return it to the testing process. Do not use it on any job.

equipmentAndPpe: Gloves suitable for handling bags, filters, attachments and the machine body, worn at all times.
Full enclosed footwear with slip-resistant soles.
Eye protection when dust or product spray is present.
Test and tag label on every machine, visible from the operating position.
Equipment register kept current with test dates and next due dates.
Cable covers or a marked route for any flex that crosses a walkway.
Protective device at the socket, confirmed before use.

commonErrors.error: Plugging in before the socket is switched off, or unplugging before it is switched off.
commonErrors.prevention: Socket off, plug in, switch on. Reverse the sequence at the end of the task.

commonErrors.error: Running a machine with a taped or cut flex because the job is almost finished.
commonErrors.prevention: Stop, unplug, tag, report. Do not tape a damaged flex.

commonErrors.error: Assuming a test label means the machine is safe on the day.
commonErrors.prevention: A test is a point in time. Check the machine each time before use, as damage can happen after testing.

commonErrors.error: Leaving the flex across a walkway or in water.
commonErrors.prevention: Route the cable behind you and keep it out of wet areas and walkways.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: The source refers to PAT testing. Check the applicable standard, the test interval and who may perform the test before you rely on any of these details.

Repairs to fixed wiring, power points, switchboards or building circuits are licensed electrical work. Only a person holding the required licence may do that work. This lesson does not grant or describe any electrical licence, and cleaners must not repair or reconnect building wiring.
Lifting machines is a manual handling task. Use the team lifting method and any lifting aid the business provides.
Before you use a machine on wet floors, check the manufacturer's rating for wet use. The rating is set by the manufacturer and is not assumed in this lesson.

qualityStandard: Pre-use check completed and recorded for every machine, with the test label date read and checked.
Socket-off connection and disconnection sequence performed without prompting.
No faulty machine used; each faulty machine tagged and reported.
No flex left crossing an active walkway or in standing water during the task.
documentationEvidence: Pre-use check record with the test label date and any defect found.
Equipment register entry showing the test label, next due date and location of the machine.
Fault tag and report to the line manager, with time and machine identifier.
summary: Check the test label, flex, plug, casing and filter before every use.
Socket off before plugging in, and socket off before unplugging.
Keep the cable behind you and out of walkways and wet areas.
A fault means the machine stops, is tagged and is reported. Repairs go to an approved person.

knowledgeChecks.question: Before you use an electrical cleaning machine, which check comes first?
options: Confirm the test label and read the next due date
Run the machine on the carpet briefly to listen to it
Wrap any visible tape around the flex to secure it

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the correct order when you finish using a machine?
options: Switch the socket off, then unplug the machine
Unplug the machine, then switch the socket off
Leave the socket on so the machine can cool down

knowledgeChecks.question: A machine has a small cut in its flex. What is the right action?
options: Tape the cut and keep working until the whole job is finished
Use it on the lowest speed until the job is finished and then check the flex
Tag the machine as faulty, unplug it and report it to your line manager
